title: But Few Among the Carnal Wise
description: But Few Among the Carnal Wise in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 96, headed “Election excludes boasting, 1 Cor. 1. 26-31”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: But few a-mong the car-nal wise, But few of no-ble race, Ob-tain the fa-vour of thine eyes, Al-might-y King of Grace.

lines: But few among the carnal wise,
Obtain the favour of thine eyes,
He takes the men of meanest name
For sons and heirs of God;
And thus he pours abundant shame
He calls the fool, and makes him know
Nature has all its glories lost
No flesh shall in his presence boast

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
